{{Youmay|the phrase "wild bantha chase"|the similar phrase "[[wild gundark chase]]"}}
{{Quote|Here, you can hurt the Empire far more than in you're gallivanting across the starlanes on some wild bantha chase.|[[Tuden Sal]] to [[Jax Pavan]]|<ref name="The Last Jedi">''[[The Last Jedi (novel)|The Last Jedi]]''</ref>}}
'''Wild bantha chase'''<ref name="Episode III">{{Film|III}}</ref> or '''wild bantha hunt'''<ref name="Ruins of Dantooine">''[[Star Wars Galaxies: The Ruins of Dantooine]]''</ref> was a [[List of phrases and slang/Legends|slang phrase]] used in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], which referred to an ultimately pointless activity which distracted someone from a desired objective.<ref name="Episode III">{{Film|III}}</ref> The idiom referred to the [[Bantha/Legends|bantha]], a pack animal from [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref>

When [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] was sent to [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]] to search for [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] at the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Gender/Legends|he]] described the hunt to [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] as possibly being "just a wild bantha chase" when Skywalker expressed his opinion that Kenobi would need his help on the mission.<ref name="Episode III" />

{{Stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
The phrase is derived from the real-world idiom "[[wild goose]] chase,"<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/wild-goose-chase|text=wild goose chase|quote='a search for something that is impossible for you to find or that does not exist, that makes you waste a lot of time|work=[[Wikipedia:Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary|''Oxford Learner's Dictionary'']]|archivedate=20260121163924}}</ref> which also exists in [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] continuity.<ref name="SW 30">[[Star Wars (1977) 30|''Star Wars'' (1977) 30]]</ref>
